name: W25Q128JVPIM
title: 128M-bit serial flash: SPI, dual/quad SPI, QPI and DTR reads
summary: W25Q128JV is a 16 Mbyte serial flash on a single 2.7 V to 3.6 V supply. It is read and written over SPI, dual SPI, quad SPI or QPI at up to 133 MHz, with double-transfer-rate reads up to 66 MHz, and it can be erased by 4KB sector, 32KB or 64KB block, or whole chip. Protection comes from status-register block protection or per-block locks, a write-protect pin and a power-up lock-out; a 64-bit unique ID, three 256-byte OTP-lockable security registers and an SFDP table are built in. It comes in 8-pin SOIC, 8-pad WSON, 16-pin SOIC and 24-ball TFBGA packages for -40 °C to +85 °C or +105 °C.

operation.text: Out of power-up or a software reset the part speaks SPI: single-line (DI in, DO out), dual (IO0-IO1) and quad (IO0-IO3) transfers are all available, with SPI modes 0 and 3. Mode 0 idles CLK low at the /CS edges, mode 3 idles it high. Quad transfers need QE=1, which turns /WP into IO2 and /HOLD into IO3. QPI is a separate state entered with 38h (only when QE=1) and left with FFh or a reset; in QPI the opcode itself also travels on four lines, two clocks per byte. SPI and QPI never run at once.

An instruction starts on the falling edge of /CS and ends on its rising edge. Bits are taken MSB first on rising CLK edges. A read may be ended after any bit; a program, erase or register write is carried out only if /CS rises right after a complete byte, which guards against stray writes. While a program, erase or status write runs, the part ignores everything except Read Status Register (and Suspend).

The DTR read instructions (0Dh, BDh, EDh, and 0Eh in QPI) latch the opcode on rising edges only, then take address and give data on both clock edges. DTR clock limits are 66 MHz at 3.0-3.6 V and 52 MHz at 2.7-3.0 V.

Read Data (03h) runs to 50 MHz, has no dummy clocks and exists only in standard SPI. Fast Read (0Bh) and the dual/quad output reads (3Bh, 6Bh) add 8 dummy clocks and run at full FR. Fast Read Dual I/O (BBh) and Quad I/O (EBh) take the address on 2 or 4 lines; EBh needs 4 dummy clocks in SPI. DTR Fast Read (0Dh) uses 6 dummy clocks. Every read auto-increments the address, so one instruction can stream the whole array; a read issued while BUSY=1 is ignored. Before the first output clock of a multi-line read the host must release the IO lines.

The dual and quad I/O reads carry mode bits M7-M0 after the address. If M5-M4 = 1,0, the following read of the same kind skips the opcode and starts straight with the address, saving eight clocks per access (XIP). Any other value returns to normal framing. To leave the mode for certain, clock FFh on IO0 (8 clocks) for EBh, FFFFh (16 clocks) for BBh, FFh/3FFh for EDh, FFFFh/FFFFFh for BDh, so that M4 reads 1.

Set Burst with Wrap (77h, SPI only) arms the quad I/O reads (EBh, EDh) to wrap inside an 8, 16, 32 or 64-byte slice of a 256-byte page, starting at the given address; W4=0 enables wrapping and W6-W5 pick its length. W4 is 1 (no wrap) after power-up or reset. In QPI, wrapping is done by the dedicated 0Ch (and DTR 0Eh) instruction instead, with length set by Set Read Parameters or carried over from 77h.

Set Read Parameters (C0h) works only in QPI. P5-P4 choose 2, 4, 6 or 8 dummy clocks for QPI 0Bh, EBh and 0Ch, each with a higher frequency ceiling; P1-P0 choose the wrap length. Defaults are 2 dummy clocks and 8 bytes. The dummy count has to be set again every time the part moves from SPI into QPI. In QPI the mode bits of EBh and EDh count as dummy clocks. Moving between SPI and QPI keeps WEL, suspend state and wrap length.

Page Program (02h) and Quad Input Page Program (32h) write 1 to 256 bytes into erased (FFh) cells, after a Write Enable (06h). /CS stays low for the whole data stream. Bytes that run past byte 255 wrap to byte 0 of that same page; to fill a whole page begin with A7-A0 = 0. A partial write leaves the other bytes of that page untouched so long as it stops before byte 255 is passed. When /CS rises the self-timed cycle (tPP) begins; BUSY reads 1 until it ends, then WEL clears. 32h mainly helps hosts clocking below about 5 MHz, since the program time dwarfs the transfer time at faster clocks.

Sector Erase (20h, 4KB), Block Erase (52h, 32KB; D8h, 64KB) and Chip Erase (C7h or 60h) set the region to FFh after a Write Enable. Each runs self-timed for tSE, tBE1, tBE2 or tCE once /CS rises, with BUSY = 1 meanwhile and WEL cleared at the end. An erase touching any protected area is not carried out; Chip Erase is refused if any region is protected.

75h interrupts a running sector erase, block erase or page program, so other locations can be read (or, during an erase suspend, programmed). It is accepted only when SUS=0 and BUSY=1, and is ignored during Chip Erase. Within tSUS BUSY falls to 0 and SUS goes to 1. During erase suspend the status write and all erases are refused; during program suspend the status write and all programs are refused. 7Ah resumes (accepted only with SUS=1, BUSY=0): SUS clears at once and BUSY returns within 200 ns. Allow tSUS between a resume and the next suspend. Power loss while suspended resets the part, clears SUS, and may corrupt the suspended page, sector or block.

Three 8-bit status registers are read with 05h, 35h and 15h (at any time, even while busy, and repeatedly while /CS stays low) and written with 01h, 31h and 11h. A non-volatile write needs 06h first and takes tW with BUSY = 1. A volatile write is preceded by 50h instead: WEL stays 0, BUSY stays 0 and the new value applies within tSHSL2; it is lost at power-off or reset, when the non-volatile values return. Writing 01h with two data bytes loads registers 1 and 2 together; with one byte only register 1 changes. QE cannot be changed while in QPI. Reserved bits read as 0 or 1 and should be ignored.

With WPS=0, BP2-BP0 pick how much of the array is read-only, TB picks top (0) or bottom (1), SEC picks 64KB blocks (0) or 4KB sectors (1), and CMP=1 inverts the chosen area. With WPS=1 these bits are ignored and the individual locks apply instead: one lock bit per 64KB block for blocks 1-254 and one per 4KB sector in the top and bottom blocks. The individual locks are volatile and all set to 1 at power-up or reset; 39h unlocks one, 36h locks one, 3Dh reads one (LSB 1 = locked), 7Eh locks all and 98h unlocks all, each lock or unlock after a Write Enable.

SRP and SRL decide who may write the status registers: software only (SRP=0), the /WP pin (SRP=1: /WP low locks, high allows), a lock until the next power cycle (SRL=1), or a permanent one-time lock entered through a special AAh, 55h prefix. /WP control works only in standard and dual SPI, since QE=1 takes the pin for IO2.

Below VWI the part holds itself in reset and accepts nothing. Above VWI program, erase, Write Enable and status-write instructions stay blocked for tPUW; reads are allowed after VCC reaches its minimum and tVSL passes. The part wakes with WEL = 0, and WEL clears again after every program, erase or register write. /CS must follow VCC on the way up and down; a pull-up on /CS achieves that.

In standard and dual SPI with QE=0 and HOLD/RST=0, /HOLD low pauses an instruction while /CS is low: DO floats and DI and CLK are ignored, so the bus can serve another device and the transfer can carry on later. Hold begins at the falling /HOLD edge if CLK is low, otherwise at the next falling CLK edge, and ends the same way on the rising /HOLD edge. Keep /CS low for the whole hold or the internal state resets.

Software reset is 66h followed directly by 99h, in SPI or QPI; any other instruction between them cancels it. The part then needs about tRST = 30 µs and accepts nothing meanwhile. Reset drops all volatile settings: volatile status bits, WEL, suspend state, read parameters, continuous read mode and wrap. On 8-pin parts the IO3 pin acts as /RESET when HOLD/RST=1 and QE=0; SOIC-16 and TFBGA have a dedicated /RESET pin that ignores QE and HOLD/RST (on SOIC-16 it has an internal pull-up and may be left open). /RESET low for 1 µs resets the part, overriding every other input and aborting any program or erase, which can corrupt data. Check BUSY and SUS before a reset.

B9h puts the part into its lowest-current state within tDP (1 µA typical). In power-down only ABh is recognised, not even Read Status, which also makes power-down a strong write lock. ABh alone wakes the part within tRES1; ABh with three dummy bytes also returns the device ID (17h) and the part is ready after tRES2. ABh is ignored while BUSY=1. The part always powers up in standby, not in power-down.

9Fh returns the JEDEC manufacturer ID EFh, memory type 70h and capacity 18h. 90h, 92h and 94h return EFh and device ID 17h, on 1, 2 or 4 lines, repeating while clocked. 4Bh followed by four dummy bytes returns a factory-set 64-bit ID unique to each part. 5Ah reads the 256-byte SFDP table (JESD216), with A23-A8 = 0 and 8 dummy clocks.

Three 256-byte security registers, separate from the main array, are erased with 44h, programmed with 42h (1 to 256 bytes) and read with 48h (8 dummy clocks, address wraps within the register). Erase and program need a Write Enable and take tSE and tPP. Setting LB1, LB2 or LB3 makes the matching register read-only for good.
DRV1-DRV0 set the read output driver to 100%, 75%, 50% or 25% strength; 25% is the default.
At least 100,000 program-erase cycles per sector and more than 20 years of data retention.

The WSON exposed pad has no internal connection; it may float or join GND. No exposed PCB vias should sit under it. On the TFBGA the ball land is 0.45 mm and the solder-mask opening 0.35 mm; a PCB ball land of 0.35 mm or less is suggested.
